title: Microscope Slides in Motion — source and archive registry supplement

records.institution: Whipple Museum of the History of Science, University of Cambridge
records.collection: Charles Elcock archive of microscope slides, tools, materials, books, and ephemera
records.holdings: The Whipple catalogue describes a surviving working archive of Belfast professional slide maker Charles Elcock: large slide cabinets, mounted foraminifera, histological slides, labels, slide-making tools and supplies, staining materials, specimens awaiting preparation, printed matter, and other archival material. The principal accession is recorded as 617 parts.
records.research_use: Exceptionally dense maker-side archive for reconstructing preparation labour, materials, labels, cabinet organization, collected raw material, commercial identity, and the relation between a professional preparer's tools and finished slides.
records.access: Object record and images online; research access through the Whipple Museum.

records.institution: Naturhistorisches Museum Wien — Archiv für Wissenschaftsgeschichte
records.collection: Ferdinand I microscopic preparations and material historical sources
records.holdings: The Museum's archive preserves thousands of microscopic preparations made by Emperor Ferdinand I, including lower plants, fish and butterfly scales, minerals and other subjects. The archive explicitly treats these preparations as material historical sources and records that many remained in didactic use at the museum long after their manufacture.
records.research_use: A rare mid-nineteenth-century object archive connecting elite botanical instruction, Oskar Plössl microscopy, preparation practice, long institutional custody, and later teaching use.
records.access: Archive holdings are generally available for research after statutory closure periods and by prior appointment.

records.collection: Albert Grunow diatom collection and documentary apparatus
records.holdings: Grunow's complex diatom collection includes unmounted material, herbarium specimens, fossil samples in historical containers, microscopy slides, a catalogue of worked samples, drawings, and annotated books that carry sample numbers for illustrations. The Museum notes that these documentary layers are essential for locating type and original material.
records.research_use: High-value object↔text system for tracing how a nineteenth-century diatomist coordinated raw material, prepared slides, catalogue entries, drawings, published illustrations and later type identification.
records.access: Digitisation is ongoing; research and collection access through Herbarium W and NHM Vienna.

records.institution: Natural History Museum of Denmark, University of Copenhagen
records.collection: Cultural and science history collection, library, and botanical/geological/zoological archives
records.date_scope: pre-1900 library and historical museum archives
records.holdings: The Museum's cultural and science history collection cares for historical scientific instruments, tools, books and art objects and includes the botanical, geological and zoological archives plus a library of older books and journals published before 1900. Historical microscopes are among the instrument holdings.
records.research_use: Archival counterpart to the Copenhagen slide holdings already captured in the object survey: acquisition, museum administration, instrument use, curator correspondence, collection movements, and pre-1900 printed context can be pursued without treating collection metadata as provenance by itself.
records.access: The library and archives are temporarily closed for on-site use; enquiries are directed to the Museum archives.

records.collection: Historical microscopic preparations of Thysanoptera by Jindřich Uzel
records.holdings: The National Museum identifies the historical collection of microscopic Thysanoptera preparations by J. Uzel as an important component of its smaller-insect-order collections, alongside other historical entomological preparations.
records.research_use: Central-European endpoint for a historically named slide maker/researcher whose late-nineteenth-century preparations can be approached through museum collection structure, taxonomy, labels, and publication history.
records.access: Research access through the National Museum's entomological collections.

records.institution: Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences
records.collection: Natural-science collections including microscope slides and scientific documentation
records.holdings: The Institute describes a large natural-history collection in which microscope slides, anatomical preparations, embryos, pollen, spores and scientific documentation coexist with zoological, geological and palaeontological holdings.
records.research_use: A Belgian route for testing historical preparation holdings against departmental records, accession histories and scientific documentation. Object-level nineteenth-century identity remains to be established by subcollection rather than inferred from the aggregate collection description.
records.access: Collection research is governed by the Institute's collection access and loan procedures.

records.holdings: The Museum's herbarium and entomology collections include substantial material mounted as microscopic preparations on glass slides. The institution's natural-history collections extend back through nineteenth-century and earlier collecting traditions, although the publicly stated slide totals include later material.
records.research_use: Scandinavian collection route for separating historical subcollections from later palynological and entomological slide programmes; nineteenth-century provenance requires named-subcollection closure before object-level promotion.
records.access: Research and loan access through the relevant Swedish Museum of Natural History collection departments.
